newsitem.title: USA: Dec cash flow to US stock funds $12.22 bln - ICI.
newsitem.headline: Dec cash flow to US stock funds $12.22 bln - ICI.

text.p: Net new cash flows to stock mutual funds in December totaled $12.22 billion, the Investment Company Institute said Tuesday.

That was down slightly from the estimate of $13.5 billion made by the industry trade group just over two weeks ago in preliminary figures and well down from the $17.16 in stock fund inflows seen in November.
For all of 1996, net new cash flow into stock funds was $222.08 billion, up from $128.22 billion for all of 1995, ICI said.

Bond and income funds saw inflows of $2.80 billion in December, compared with $1.43 billion in November. For the year, flows into these funds were up $13.17 billion after an outflow of $4.81 billion in 1995.

Money market funds had inflows of $3.43 billion in December after a $15.03 billion flood of money in November. For all of 1996, money market funds had a net inflow of $89.32 billion compared with $89.41 billion in 1995.
Despite the $12.22 billion inflow into stock funds in December, the ICI said declines in domestic stock prices resulted in a decline in stock fund assets for the month.
Stock fund assets fell $11.29 billion or 0.6 percent to $1,751.96 billion in December.
Combined assets for all types of mutual funds decreased 0.2 percent or $7.86 billion to $3,540 billion in December.
